title: Fractional CEO Advice for Business Owners | Vestis Solutions
description: Fractional CEO-level advice for owner-led businesses. You stay CEO. I'm the outside partner for your biggest decisions, priorities and accountability.
h1: Fractional CEO-level advice, while you stay the CEO
intro: You make every big call alone. Pricing, hiring, cash, which project to chase. Your team brings you problems, not answers, and there's nobody to think it through with who understands the whole business. You don't need someone to take over. You need a partner in the room.
definition: A fractional CEO is usually a part-time executive brought in to run a company for a period. In an owner-led business, the more useful version is an outside executive thinking partner: the owner stays CEO, and the fractional partner helps make the big decisions, set priorities and hold everyone accountable.

sections.h2: An honest take on the fractional CEO role
paras: Some fractional CEOs step in and run the company. That makes sense when an owner is leaving or a board needs a temporary leader. That's not what I do.
You built the business, and you stay in charge. I work beside you as an outside executive, someone who has seen business from both sides of the desk and will tell you what he sees, plainly.

sections.h2: What fractional CEO support looks like each month
paras: We meet for four 30-minute owner sessions a month, with support between calls. Each session goes to the one or two decisions that matter most right now.
bullets: Priorities: what to fix first, and what to say no to
Hiring: when to add a salesperson or office manager, and what the role is
Numbers to watch: the few figures that tell you if the week went well
Culture and leadership: clear values and a weekly meeting that holds people accountable
Accountability for you: we agree on what you'll do, and I'll ask about it next week

paras: I'll help you think through cash flow, pricing and growth. I don't give legal, tax or accounting advice. When a decision touches your entity type, taxes or contracts, that part goes to your CPA or attorney, and I'll help you bring them the right questions.

sections.h2: Who I am and how to start
paras: For over a decade I worked in banking and finance with business owners through cash crunches, growing pains and big wins. Then I co-founded a company with a partner and lived it myself. I'm based in Charlotte, NC, and work with owners locally and across the US.

Partnerships start at $3,000 a month and also include getting found on Google and in AI answers, plus a sales process review. We start with 90 days, then go month to month. The first step is a free 30-minute fit call.

faq.q: What does a fractional CEO do?
faq.a: A fractional CEO provides part-time executive leadership, either running the company for a period or advising the owner who runs it. I do the second. You stay CEO, and I help you decide what matters most, set priorities, plan key hires and hold the team, and you, accountable.

faq.q: Will a fractional CEO take over my business?
faq.a: Not in my case, you stay the CEO and make the final call. I act as your outside executive thinking partner. Some fractional CEOs do step in to run a company, but that fits a different situation, such as an owner leaving or a board needing an interim leader.

faq.q: Is a fractional CEO the same as a business coach?
faq.a: They overlap, but a fractional CEO partner works inside the actual decisions of your business, not only on your mindset. I look at your numbers, your sales process and your systems, help put changes in place, and review results with you every 30 days.

faq.q: How much does a fractional CEO cost?
faq.a: Fractional CEO pricing varies widely by role and hours. My partnerships start at $3,000 a month, which includes four 30-minute owner sessions plus SEO and AEO work and a sales process review. We start with 90 days, then continue month to month.

faq.q: Can you help with taxes, contracts or business structure?
faq.a: I can help you think through the business side of those decisions, but I don't give legal, tax or accounting advice. Entity type, taxes and contracts go to your CPA or attorney. I'll help you get clear on the questions before you meet with them.

faq.q: When should an owner get outside executive help?
faq.a: Get outside help when you're the bottleneck for every decision and growth has stalled because of it. Other signs are a key hire you keep putting off or a team that waits on you. An outside partner gives you a second set of experienced eyes without a full-time executive salary.
